rules: Every record remains a candidate until human review.
Similarity does not imply historical descent, common origin, or diffusion.
Publication and index dates are preserved separately; indexing novelty is not publication novelty.
Human remains and mortuary contexts require cultural-sensitivity review.
Biological material identification does not by itself establish symbolic, ritual, religious, or semantic meaning.
Containerized or unusual human-remains context does not by itself establish intentional burial or ritual deposition.
Biomedical or psychiatric correlation is not evidence of historical diagnosis or identity.

new_candidates.title: Three thousand five hundred years of sheeppox virus evolution inferred from archaeological and codicological genomes
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Recovers sheeppox-virus genomes from medieval parchment and Bronze Age sheep teeth, demonstrating that manuscript material can function as a biological archive in addition to a textual source. This broadens NOEMA source ontology for historical documents and material culture.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Pathogen DNA in parchment records source-animal biology and production history, not the manuscript text's religious meaning, author community, or ritual function. Virus detected on non-sheep parchment may reflect cross-species infection or production contamination.

provenance.source: Science Advances; University College Dublin public research release

new_candidates.title: Equal in death: Ancient genomic analysis of children's early Christian burials
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Genomic screening of 142 late-Viking/medieval individuals in Sweden found that children interred with adults in collective graves rarely shared close biological ties; burial spatial patterns also showed sex/gender-pattern structure with flexibility. Useful for separating co-burial, kinship and social organization.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Biological relatedness does not exhaust social kinship, and burial spatial pattern does not by itself establish theology, belief, or prescribed Christian doctrine.

new_candidates.title: Beyond animal glue: Paleoproteomic analysis of paint binders and adhesives in ancient Egypt
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Proteomics identifies animal collagen and previously undocumented plant proteins including sesame and moringa in painted Egyptian artifacts dating roughly 1425 BCE-400 CE. It creates source-bounded material-composition observations that can later be compared with textual and iconographic evidence.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Chemical or biological identification of a material does not establish why it was selected. Proposed symbolic or religious significance requires independent contextual/textual evidence.

new_candidates.title: Human remains discovered inside a dolium in a gate tower at Roman Deultum, Bulgaria
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: A man was found inside a large storage vessel in a burned gate-tower context with knives still on his person. Excavator interpretation reported publicly is that he may have hidden during an attack rather than having been intentionally interred. This is a useful negative-control case for burial/ritual classification.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Public field report only. Do not label as burial, sacrifice, ritual deposition, or funerary practice without primary excavation publication and contextual analysis.

provenance.source: Archaeology Magazine reporting Archaeologia Bulgarica / Bulgarian Academy of Sciences excavation
